chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Hammad ibn Isa from Abdullah ibn Abi Ya'fur from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
Regarding the man who marries a female slave from among his female slaves, and with him in the house is someone who sees it and hears it, he said: 'There is no objection.'
ai.seo_question: Is it permissible for a master to marry his own female slave in the presence of others?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the validity of marrying a female slave (jariyah) from one's own possession even when a third party is present and aware, affirming the permissibility of such unions within the domestic sphere. It highlights the flexibility in marital contracts for concubines compared to free women, reflecting the socio-legal context of early Islamic society where ownership and marriage were intertwined. The ruling underscores that the presence of a witness does not invalidate the contract, emphasizing the master's authority in this specific legal category.
